quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if it is safe to move.

questions.question: If you find yourself riding next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in the vehicle's blind spot. If you are stuck next to another vehicle, speed up or slow down to move away from it.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of riding experience.
Are caused by faulty ignition systems.
Occur because of distractions from passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of riding experience.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a motorcycle new to you. Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should be placed:

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the lead rider. This allows more experienced riders to watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white background and black letters are regulatory signs. They tell you the rules of the road, like speed limits. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: Your body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If a person consumed eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: To find how many drinks remain, subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks still in the body.

questions.question: To be effective, a face shield should not:
questions.correctAnswerText: Be airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be clear, protect your face, allow side vision, and fit securely. It should allow air to flow through. An airtight shield will fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast that hits you, you will have the most control if you are riding:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most room on both sides if a wind blast pushes you.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can stop other vehicles from squeezing into their lane by:

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Making angry faces at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other vehicles from trying to share your space.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is not as strong as the rear brake.
It is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use when used correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.question: What reduces the effects of alcohol in your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver burns alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed up this process. The only way to reduce alcohol's effects is to wait and let your body remove it.

questions.question: What is in the center portion of a lane?

options.text: It is always the best part of the lane for a motorcycle.
Oil and grease are often there, but it is usually safe to ride.
Oil and grease are there, and it is never safe to ride.
It is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oil and grease are often there, but it is usually safe to ride.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars collect in a strip down the center of each lane. Unless the road is wet, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. However, avoid large buildups of oil and grease found at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: What can happen if you brake too hard?

options.text: You lose grip on one or both wheels.
It takes too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose grip on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you may lose grip on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake, squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: When should a motorcyclist shift gears?

options.text: By changing power suddenly in a turn.
While riding the brake through a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before a turn.
questions.explanation: Shift gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: What happens if your front tire goes flat while riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: The steering feels heavy.
questions.explanation: If your front tire goes flat, the steering will feel heavy. If steering feels heavy, pull off the road and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This includes wet pavement, low visibility, or heavy traffic where another driver may cut in front of you.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of proper lane position?
questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: The faster you drink, what happens?

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
Your body removes the alcohol faster.
The effects of alcohol are less noticeable.
You are less likely to get pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink fast, more alcohol builds up in your body. It is never safe to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: At night, how should your following distance compare to daytime?

options.text: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead at night.
Leave less space between you and the vehicle ahead at night.
Keep the same following distance day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances because you cannot see shadows or light contrasts. Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead at night than you do during the day.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Lean in the same direction as the operator.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the same direction as the operator.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane behind a car:

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you without checking the side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you without checking the side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more than their side mirrors. This position helps you stay visible.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They let you see all the way to the sides as needed.
You do not have to wear one if you think it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They let you see all the way to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that a helmet limits side vision, but this is not true. Any approved helmet allows you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
